[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Flask-SQLAlchemy Integration Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this tutorial, you will learn how to integrate Flask-SQLAlchemy into a Flask application. Flask-SQLAlchemy is an extension that adds support for SQLAlchemy to your Flask application, simplifying database interactions using Object Relational Mapping (ORM)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, you need to install Flask and Flask-SQLAlchemy using pip. Run the following command in your terminal:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install Flask Flask-SQLAlchemy"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configuring the Application"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, create a basic Flask application and configure the database URI. The database URI tells Flask-SQLAlchemy where to find your database. For this example, we will use a local SQLite database."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///site.db'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
db = SQLAlchemy(app)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Defining Models"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Models represent your database tables as Python classes. Each attribute of the class corresponds to a column in the table. Let us create a simple User model."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"class User(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Creating the Database"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To create the database and tables defined by your models, you can use the Flask interactive Python shell. Run the following commands in your terminal:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"python
>>> from app import app, db
>>> with app.app_context():
...     db.create_all()
..."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Performing CRUD Operations"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once your database and models are set up, you can perform Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations. Here is how to add a new user:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"with app.app_context():
    new_user = User(username='john_doe', email='john@example.com')
    db.session.add(new_user)
    db.session.commit()"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"To query all users from the database, use the query attribute provided by SQLAlchemy:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"with app.app_context():
    users = User.query.all()
    print(users)"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Flask-SQLAlchemy simplifies database setup and ORM management in Flask."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Models are mapped to Python classes inheriting from db.Model."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Database context must be active using app.app_context() when performing database operations outside of requests."}]
